Yaltushkiv Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. This, the older of Yaltushkiv's Jewish cemeteries, was established in the 18th century; according to local testimony, it was partly demolished by Nazi troops during WWII, with the remaining tombstones later gathered into a single pile and fenced, and trees planted on the demolished section in the 1970s. A locked ohel dating to 1791 survives on the site, its key hidden under a nearby stone. Yaltushkiv's Jewish community, first recorded in 1784, reached 1,238 of 3,533 residents (about a third) by 1897; on October 15, 1942, 1,194 Jews from Yaltushkiv and the surrounding area were executed in a single action.
